newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Police foil Colombian cocaine kings' jailbreak.
newsitem.headline: Police foil Colombian cocaine kings' jailbreak.

text.p: Police foiled an apparent jailbreak attempt on Wednesday by Colombia's billionaire cocaine kings, the Rodriguez Orejuela brothers, officials said.

Police intelligence officers, acting on a tip-off, discovered a number of loose blocks in the wall of a kitchen in the high-security wing of Bogota's La Picota prison where the former chiefs of the Cali drug mob are held.
It was not immediately clear how Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela, who once controlled an estimated 80 percent of the world's cocaine supply, planned to make their getaway, police said.
"Police intelligence services uncovered an escape plan by the two Rodriguez Orejuela brothers. I cannot reveal any more details at this stage," a National Police spokesman said.
Rafael Lamo, head of the National Prisons Institute (INPEC), said it was premature to talk of a full-blown escape plan.
"This is a reaction of everybody deprived of their liberty. There are moments of desperation and all inmates have anxiety attacks," Lamo told reporters.
Earlier this week, police cancelled one of the brothers' hospital visits. Both suffer from heart problems and receive regular check-ups at a private clinic in northern Bogota.
The brothers were captured in 1995 and were sentenced earlier this year to jail terms that could see them walk free in little more than five years.
